<p class="micro-label">PROFILE / 2026</p>

# Niansia

<p class="role-line">Computer science graduate preparing for graduate study in AI security, computer vision, and vision-language models.</p>

I graduated in 2026 with a degree in Computer Science from **Yuan Ze University** and am currently preparing applications to graduate programs. My interests center on the security, robustness, and reasoning capabilities of visual and multimodal intelligent systems.

I am especially interested in how evidence is collected, how reasoning fails, how uncertainty is communicated, and how experiments can be reproduced by other researchers.

::: {.section-block #research}
::: {.section-rail}
<h2>Research areas</h2>
:::

::: {.section-content}
<p class="section-lead">My current interests are organized around two closely related research areas.</p>

::: {.question-list}
::: {.question-item}
<span class="question-index">A</span>
<div>
<h3>AI &amp; multimodal security</h3>
<p>How can visual and multimodal AI systems remain secure, robust, and auditable under adversarial inputs, weak evidence, and real-world uncertainty?</p>
<p class="keywords">Security / robustness / adversarial and failure analysis / content integrity / trustworthy evaluation</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.question-item}
<span class="question-index">B</span>
<div>
<h3>Vision &amp; multimodal intelligence</h3>
<p>How can computer vision and vision-language systems preserve visual evidence, reason across modalities and time, and be evaluated for grounding rather than fluency alone?</p>
<p class="keywords">Computer vision / VLMs / multimodal reasoning / memory / evaluation</p>
</div>
:::
:::

<p class="quiet-note"><strong>Additional interests.</strong> Quantitative machine learning, interactive systems, and research software.</p>

<p class="quiet-note">Some active research projects remain private during development and review; code, results, and reproducible artifacts will be released when appropriate.</p>
:::
:::
